_note: What each tag that a rule reads does, shown in hover tooltips (with any owned relic keyed on it). Relic effects keyed on tags (foe_damage, foe_spoils, gear_bonus, node_yield in data/relics.json) count as reading them. Any entity can carry tags in its data ("tags": [...] on enemies, hero classes, traits, townsfolk roles, buildings, item bases or relics; see Content.TAG_KINDS). Descriptive tags no rule reads yet are fine and show by name alone. When a rule starts reading a tag, add its line here: tests/test_tags.gd fails until you do. Prize tags (a building's "prize", like the hunting lodge's beast prize) are explained from data/buildings.json, so they need no line.
trophy: a fearsome foe heroes boast of; Trophy wall and the Trophy-king's crown give lasting gifts when it falls
swift: a swift townsperson; Swiftfoot anklet makes them carry more and gather faster
sentient: turns on whoever hits it, watch posts and the keep included; Taunting drum keeps it on a tower that shot it twice as long
courier: sends tribespeople from the town to carry provisions out to heroes in the wilds who run low
fighter: stands and fights, so it counts toward the town's power level; Horde drum makes fighters stronger the more there are
siege: ignores people and heads for gates and the hearth; beating an attack made of them offers their spoils
plant: grows back; a Forester's hut nearby makes it regrow faster; Thorn-witch's veil brings more from it and makes it regrow, and on a near plate (the Greenwood) it and the Lookout cairn change its numbers
human: Turncoat's torc may turn it to your side when it falls; Kinslayer's brand strikes it harder; Barrow-king's lamp takes a bone from it; beating an attack made of them offers their spoils; Bloodied banner gives heroes more XP from it
beast: Hunter's blood-mark strikes it harder, butchers it for food and hides and keeps it off townsfolk unless they strike first; Wolfmother's fang bites it harder; beating an attack made of them offers their spoils; the Horn of the wild hunt strikes it harder, butchers it and gives heroes double XP from it
undead: Barrow-king's lamp doubles the damage it takes and takes its bones; the reliquary and Barrow-king's ring strike it harder; beating an attack made of them offers their spoils
wet: wet ground: on a near plate (the Fen), Bog-drowner's stake and the Causeway change how fast it is crossed; Bog-drowner's stake also doubles what gatherers bring from wet nodes (bog iron)
grave: a near plate of old graves (the Barrow): Barrow-king's lamp keeps its dead down and doubles its grave goods
staple: always in a run's blueprint pool, whatever else the run deals
bold: spars with other bold heroes in a Duelling ring each dawn, learning fast but getting hurt; on the attack's dusk goes out to meet it on the plate it crosses; Glory-hound's banner doubles its shells for kills on the turning ring
barter: a caravan deal that swaps your goods for others; the caravan offers it more when you hold its goods twice over, and Haggler's scales makes it bring more
metal: a caravan deal for metal or metalwork; the caravan offers it more while a tool set of your age is still unbought
pact: a strong relic with a real cost, offered every fourth round
spoils: taken from a beaten warband: offered beside the relics after an attack made of its kind
proud: sleeping rough sours their mood twice as fast; wearing steel cheers them
fire: sets the hearth's and watch posts' shots alight, so they light up the night
mystic: a worker of dark rites; Barrow-king's lamp strikes it harder
stone: stone gear, or stony ground for gatherers; Cairn-warden's cord favours both, and on a near plate (the Stonefield) it and the Lookout cairn change its numbers
bone: bone gear; Barrow-king's lamp strengthens it, and heroes then favour it
hide: hide gear; Hunter's blood-mark strengthens it, and heroes then favour it
bronze: bronze gear; Smith-god's hammer strengthens it, and heroes then favour it
iron: iron and steel gear; Smith-god's hammer strengthens it, and heroes then favour it
ore: ore ground (copper, tin, bog iron); Smith-god's hammer brings more from it
